summary: The useful test at Utah is whether the backfield can keep the offense on schedule while the defense handles a runner who can also catch. Protect possessions and make the trip a sustained effort.

items.headline: Cummings-Coleman’s move adds another backfield option
items.tldr: The defensive back scored on the ground against Middle Tennessee. His future role still depends on ball security and learning the offense; watch the actual rotation.

items.headline: Edwards delivered 137 rushing yards and three touchdowns
items.tldr: The Middle Tennessee game showed he could carry a larger workload. Watch whether the blocking gives him a useful first cut against Utah.

items.headline: Kansas heads west after holding Middle Tennessee to 138 total yards
items.tldr: That completed-game result sets up a tougher test. Watch the defense finish tackles and avoid giving away a long gain after initial contact.

items.headline: Utah’s Parker has scored as both runner and receiver
items.tldr: Utah’s preview lists touchdowns in both roles. Account for him after the snap, especially when a short throw can replace a running play.

items.headline: Kansas–Kansas State is set for 11 a.m. CT on October 17
items.tldr: FS1 will carry the game in Manhattan. First comes the late trip to Utah; plan for the quick change in viewing time the following week.

lead.headline: Keep options open.
lead.body: Find a useful gain before the defense knows the next call. On the other side, account for the back when he leaves the backfield.

matchup.question: What should Kansas emphasize this week?
matchup.answer: At Utah, watch the backfield workload, protection and coverage of the running back.
